summary: The settlement stall is caused by a schema-breaking order-service release: dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, deployed 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity and stamped a v2 schema header, while settlement-service remained on schema v1 and was never upgraded (F1, F33, F34). The first affected record at orders-3@8841207 fails to deserialize with the explicit v1/v2 mismatch error ~2m14s after the deploy (F8, F14), is retried as a poison message in a tight loop tens of thousands of times, blocks partition orders-3 so no offsets commit, and drives lag monotonically from ~1.5k to ~59k with zero settlements posted (F7, F9, F10). Competing hypotheses are contradicted by evidence: the poll-config change cfg-3004 cannot produce a schema error (F18), broker telemetry is flat and the other broker consumer is unaffected (F11, F12, F29), and ledger-db shows no contention through onset (F28). Confidence is medium (0.70) rather than high because the same-broker hop is verified but the same-topic/producer-id hop is permanently unverifiable and the log-signature set is truncated.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema-breaking deploy (qty->quantity) poisons settlement consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (07:40:00Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty -> quantity and stamped schema header v2 without keeping the legacy field. settlement-service, still on schema v1 (never upgraded; F34), fails to deserialize the first affected OrderExecuted record at orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', 07:42:14Z). The record is treated as a poison message and retried in a tight loop (tens of thousands of attempts), blocking partition orders-3, so no offsets commit, lag grows monotonically (~1.5k -> ~59k) and zero settlements post. The origin of the fault is the schema-breaking code release, not the consumer's poll settings.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 deploys order-service v2.16.0 renaming OrderExecuted qty->quantity, adding field venue, and adding a v2 schema header; it is the only deployment across all services between 06:00-09:59Z and is still live with no rollback

The only other change near onset is the settlement-service poll-config change cfg-3004 (07:35Z), which reduces batch size 500->200 and cannot produce a schema error; no broker/order-service/kafka config or flag change exists in the window, so the schema change reaches the broker only through the code deploy

order-service has a queue-produce edge to the same shared kafka component that settlement-service consumes from (queue-consume), and both write the shared ledger-db; the dependency graph only resolves to the 'kafka' component node, not per-topic nodes, so order-service and settlement-service are confirmed to share the broker but not confirmed to share the exact topic orders-3

settlement-service's consumer receives an OrderExecuted record with header v2 but no qty field and fails deserialization at 07:42:14Z, ~2m14s after the deploy and ~7m14s after the poll change; settlement-service was never upgraded to schema v2
The record becomes a poison message retried in a tight loop on partition orders-3@8841207 (attempt counters in the tens of thousands), blocking the partition and preventing offset commits
No offsets commit -> consumer lag rises monotonically from ~1572 to ~59267 (max 61605) and zero settlements post
settlement-service CPU doubles from ~28% to ~70% at the same onset, consistent with the retry loop rather than an external load spike

assumptions: The events settlement-service consumes are produced by order-service: the graph only resolves to the shared 'kafka' component, and get_service_dependencies for settlement-service reached depth 2 with no producer edge enumerated, so the producer of the consumed topic is not directly verified.

The v2-schema record at orders-3@8841207 was actually produced by order-service v2.16.0; no producer-id / record-header metadata for that offset was retrieved (tc-047 budget_exhausted) and no schema-registry event evidences the v2 header's origin.
A single undeserializable record is sufficient to block partition orders-3 and prevent commits for all later records, matching the observed tight retry loop.

The absence of rebalance/assignment-loss or offset-commit-failure signatures is inferred from a truncated result (40 of 81 returned, 40 of 409 matched ERROR entries) with a WARN+ filter that could suppress consumer-group WARN signatures; competing signatures are not positively excluded.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Schema mismatch originates from an unverified producer / registry event, not necessarily order-service v2.16.0
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The observed failure is a schema-version mismatch: a record on the consumed path carries header v2 while settlement-service deserializes as v1. dep-6010 is only the most plausible source of that v2 header. An alternate origin exists: the v2-format record could be injected by a different producer (e.g. payment-service or another producer on the shared kafka), or a schema-registry/topic-level change not captured by the deployment/config queries could have re-labelled records. The fix would then be on the producer/registry side or a consumer schema upgrade, not rolling back dep-6010.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: kafka (shared broker / schema path; exact producer unconfirmed)

causal_chain.claim: A record with schema header v2 and no qty field reaches settlement-service's consumed path
settlement-service is still on schema v1 and cannot deserialize it, blocking the partition and growing lag

The v2 header's origin is not verified: the graph exposes only the 'kafka' component (no per-topic nodes), the producer-id/header metadata for orders-3@8841207 was never retrieved (budget exhausted), and no schema-registry change record exists in the window, so any producer on the shared broker could in principle be the source

assumptions: An unidentified producer or registry action produced the v2 record; no direct evidence of such a producer exists, only the absence of a verified producer edge for orders-3.
The registry/credential config-change gap (no query was run for schema-registry components) could hide a registry event.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared kafka broker / partition rebalance stalled settlement consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side event (rebalance, partition reassignment, maintenance) on the shared kafka cluster caused settlement-service to lose its partition assignment, stalling consumption and growing lag, mirroring HIST-112.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka component
a broker rebalance/reassignment stalls the consumer and it stops advancing offsets
lag grows monotonically and zero settlements post

assumptions: A rebalance occurred near 07:40Z despite no telemetry confirming it; the actual error signature would be assignment/commit errors, not deserialization.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No rebalance/assignment-loss or offset-commit error signature appears in the window, and the only observed signatures are deserialization failure and poison-message retries on one specific offset (F8, F9), which a rebalance would not produce. The broker is healthy: cpu_pct flat ~34-35% with no onset change (F11), under_replicated_partitions 0.0 for all 31 points and messages_in_per_s steady (F29), and notification-service on the same broker family shows no lag growth (F12). HIST-112 is a past-incident lead only and cannot carry a live hypothesis. Partially tempered by the critique: the absence of a rebalance signature is only weakly established (truncated log page, WARN+ filter, F26), but the positive, mechanism-matching deserialization evidence outweighs it.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db contention stalls settlement commits
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db (four writer services including order-service) became slow/contended, so settlement-service commits block and lag grows, with settlement as a symptom of a shared dependency bottleneck.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service writes to the shared ledger-db, which is also written by order-service, portfolio-service and payment-service
ledger-db becomes slow/contended and settlement commits block
lag grows monotonically and zero settlements post

assumptions: A latency-only DB symptom would be invisible because ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms or error_rate metric (F27); DB contention is possible but unobserved.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The visible failure is a schema/deserialization error on a specific offset (F8) and a tight poison-message retry loop (F9, F10), not commit failures or DB latency errors. ledger-db telemetry that IS available is flat through the 07:40Z onset: slow_queries_per_min 0.4-1.56 with no step change, connections_active ~58-64, cpu_pct ~28-32 (F28), and notification-service (not a DB writer on this path) is unaffected (F12). Residual caveat per critique: ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms or error_rate (F27) and replication_lag_ms/disk_used_pct were never queried, so a purely latency-only DB co-factor is not positively excluded — but it cannot explain the schema-specific error text.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service poll-config change (cfg-3004) caused the stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 07:35:00Z change to consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 on settlement-service altered consumer behavior in a way that led to the stuck partition / lag growth the reporter attributes to poll settings.

causal_chain.claim: the changed poll behavior causes the consumer to stop committing offsets / block a partition
lag grows monotonically and zero settlements post

assumptions: A smaller max.poll.records could stall a consumer; not supported by any error signature.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-3004 only reduces batch size (500->200); it cannot produce a schema/deserialization error or a single offset retried tens of thousands of times (F18), and it is settlement-service-only so it cannot produce any cross-service artifact. Every observed error signature (deserialization + poison-message, F25) belongs to a schema-mismatch mechanism rather than batching. The poll change precedes the first error by ~7m14s vs the deploy's ~2m14s, but this timing argument is only weak corroboration: the stall onset was never independently measured and the onset bucket is coarse (F7 onset between 07:30 and 07:40Z).

facts.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in 06:00-09:59Z: dep-6010, order-service v2.16.0, deployed 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, with changes 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2'.
dep-6010 remains live with rolled_back_at null, and no deployment or config change of any kind occurred after 07:42Z in the incident window (no rollback, no mitigation release).
settlement-service was never upgraded to schema v2: deployments scoped to settlement-service over 07:00-09:59Z return count 0.
The earliest settlement-service error at 07:42:14Z is a deserialization failure on orders-3@8841207: "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)".
The deploy at 07:40:00Z precedes the first error by ~2m14s, versus ~7m14s for the poll-config change at 07:35:00Z.
Poison-message retries all target the same offset orders-3@8841207 with attempt counters in the tens of thousands, indicating a single blocked partition retried in a tight loop rather than advancing.

settlement-service consumer_lag was healthy (~38-48) until 07:30Z, rose from the 07:40-07:50 bucket onward and climbed monotonically to avg 59267 / max 61605 by 09:50Z; onset falls between 07:30Z and 07:40Z.
settlement-service CPU more than doubled at the same onset (avg ~27-28% through 06:00-07:30Z to ~69-71% by 09:50Z), consistent with a retry loop burning CPU rather than external load.
The only other settlement-service config change in the window is cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35:00Z); it was never reverted and no schema-v2 consumer setting was introduced.

The poll-config change cannot produce the observed failure shape: it only reduces batch size and is settlement-service-only, so it cannot generate a schema/deserialization error or a cross-service artifact.
order-service produces to the same shared kafka that settlement-service consumes, and both write to shared ledger-db; only two changes exist near onset, dep-6010 and cfg-3004.
The broker looks healthy and not overloaded through onset: cpu_pct flat ~34-35%, under_replicated_partitions 0.0 for all 31 points in 07:30-08:00Z, messages_in_per_s steady (~2226-2734 msg/s).
notification-service, the other consumer on the shared broker, shows no lag growth over the same window (flat ~51-67 band), so the fault is not shared across all consumers.
ledger-db shows no contention at the 07:40Z onset: slow_queries_per_min flat in a 0.4-1.56 band, connections_active ~58-64, cpu_pct ~28-32, with no step change.

No kafka/broker or order-service config/flag change occurred in the window (count 0 for 06:00-07:45Z and for kafka scope), so the schema change reaches the broker only through code deployment dep-6010.

The 07:30-08:10Z settlement-service log page contains exactly two signature patterns (deserialization failure and poison-message retries), but is truncated (40 of 81 returned), so exclusivity of the signature set is not proven.
ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms and no error_rate metric, and kafka exposes only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions.

Historical incidents with identical symptoms (HIST-112 consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance; HIST-106 mTLS cert expiry; HIST-111 ledger-db slowdown affecting settlement) are leads only and no evidence in this window matches their mechanisms.

assumptions: The events settlement-service consumes are produced by order-service. The graph only resolves to the shared 'kafka' component and no producer edge for the consumed topic was enumerated, so the producer relationship is inferred from order-service's queue-produce edge and settlement-service's queue-consume edge landing on the same shared broker node (F19, F20) rather than directly verified.

The v2-schema record at orders-3@8841207 was actually produced by order-service v2.16.0. No producer-id or record-header metadata for that offset was retrieved (F21) and no schema-registry event evidences the v2 header's origin.
A single undeserializable record is sufficient to block partition orders-3 and prevent offset commits for all later records, matching the observed tight retry loop.

The absence of rebalance/assignment-loss and offset-commit-failure signatures is inferred from a truncated result (40 of 81 returned) with a WARN+ filter; competing signatures are not positively excluded (F26).
order-service and settlement-service touch the same topic (orders-3), not merely the same Kafka cluster; topic-level topology was permanently unavailable (F21).

No out-of-band mitigation (manual consumer restart, DLQ skip, offset reset) occurred, since no deployment or config change was recorded after 07:42Z (F31, F32); such an action would be invisible to the deployment/config queries.
The stall onset is between 07:30Z and 07:40Z per lag bucketing (F7); a finer onset time was not independently measured.

timeline.event: Baseline healthy: settlement-service consumer_lag ~38-48, CPU ~27-28%, kafka cpu flat ~34-35%, ledger-db slow_queries/connections/cpu flat.
Last healthy lag bucket; onset falls between this bucket and the next (07:40-07:50).
settlement-service config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records 500 -> 200 by m.das (the only settlement-service config change; never reverted).

order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) by a.khan goes live: OrderExecuted field renamed qty -> quantity, venue field added, event schema version header v2. Only deployment across all services in the window.
Same onset: settlement-service consumer_lag jumps (avg 1572 -> 5930), CPU doubles to ~60.8%; kafka and ledger-db telemetry remain flat.
First settlement-service error: deserialization failure at orders-3@8841207 - "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)".
Poison-message retry loop begins on the same offset: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked', attempt counters reach tens of thousands.
Through 09:59Z: no deployment and no config change of any kind across all services - dep-6010 not rolled back, cfg-3004 not reverted, no broker action.
settlement-service lag at avg 59267 / max 61605; CPU steady ~69-71%; zero settlements posted; notification-service lag flat ~51-67 throughout.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0) to the previous order-service release that emits the legacy 'qty' field, or re-emit OrderExecuted with both 'qty' (legacy) and 'quantity' plus a compatible schema header, so the v1 settlement-service consumer can deserialize the blocked record.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is the only change in the window that can produce the observed v1/v2 schema error (F1, F13, F16), it is still live with no rollback (F33, F31), and the mechanism is the positively observed deserialization mismatch on orders-3@8841207 (F8).

recommended_actions.action: After the producer fix, confirm recovery by verifying that offset orders-3@8841207 deserializes, the poison-message retry loop stops, offsets commit, consumer_lag returns to baseline (~40-70) and settlement CPU drops back to ~27-28%. If the blocked record cannot be replayed, reset/skip that offset under change control as a one-off.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recovery is only proven if the blocked offset clears and lag drains; the current state is lag ~59k with the offset retried tens of thousands of times and no commits (F9, F7, F10).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records) as a remediation; it is not the cause and reverting it adds an unrelated variable during recovery.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3004 only reduces batch size and cannot produce a schema deserialization error or a single blocked offset retried tens of thousands of times (F18, F25).

recommended_actions.action: Upgrade settlement-service to the v2 schema (support 'quantity'/venue and the v2 header) and add forward/backward-compatible handling: unknown-field tolerance and a dead-letter path for undeserializable records instead of a tight infinite retry loop on one offset.
recommended_actions.rationale: settlement-service was never upgraded to v2 (F34) and the absence of a DLQ/skip path is what turned one bad record into a full partition block and multi-hour outage (F8, F9).

recommended_actions.action: Release-coordinate producer schema changes: require backward-compatible evolution (keep legacy fields through at least one consumer upgrade cycle) and gated rollout of schema-version headers, with a pre-deploy check that all consumers of the shared kafka are on the new schema version.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single schema-breaking release (qty->quantity + v2 header) with no consumer upgrade path took down settlement with zero settlements for over two hours (F1, F34, F7).

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting that distinguishes poison-message/deserialization failures and per-partition offset commit stalls from generic lag, and alert on repeated retries of the same offset.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure mode (one offset retried tens of thousands of times, partition blocked) was visible in logs at 07:42-07:44Z but the incident ran ~1h40m before the report (F9, F8, F25).

recommended_actions.action: Instrument schema-registry/header provenance and per-topic producer metadata in the topology and observability tooling so a v2 header's origin can be attributed directly rather than inferred from the deploy summary.
recommended_actions.rationale: The causal chain's producer/topic hop could not be verified: the graph exposes only a 'kafka' node and the orders-3 metadata query failed with budget_exhausted (F21, F19, F20).

data_gaps: Same-topic confirmation is unavailable: the dependency graph exposes only a single 'kafka' component node with no per-topic nodes, and the orders-3 topic query returned budget_exhausted, so it cannot be confirmed that order-service and settlement-service touch the exact same topic rather than the same cluster (F21).
No producer-id or record-header metadata for orders-3@8841207 was retrieved, so the v2 header's producer is inferred from dep-6010's summary, not directly observed.

Log-signature exclusivity is unproven: the 07:30-08:10Z log result was truncated (40 of 81 returned) with a WARN+ filter, and targeted searches for 'rebalance' and 'commit' signatures failed on budget, so rebalance/assignment-loss or commit-failure signatures in the unreturned entries are not positively excluded (F26).

No schema-registry, consumer-group assignment state, or topic-partition tool exists in the toolkit; config-change queries for registry/credential components were never run, so an out-of-band registry or credential change near 07:35-07:40Z cannot be ruled in or out.

ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms or error_rate and replication_lag_ms/disk_used_pct were never queried, so a latency-only DB co-factor remains unverified (not excluded); likewise settlement-service memory and other broker metrics were unqueried.

No deployment or config record can reveal an out-of-band mitigation (manual consumer restart, offset reset, DLQ skip); the claim that nothing cleared rests on the absence of recorded interventions rather than a fresh post-08:00Z error-count query.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the v2-header record at orders-3@8841207 was produced by a service other than order-service, or that decoupling order-service's schema change (e.g. rolling back dep-6010) leaves the deserialization failure and lag growth unchanged.

Observation that the events consumed by settlement-service are produced by a different producer on the shared broker (e.g. payment-service) rather than order-service, which would replace H1 with H5 as the causal origin.
Recovery without any producer-side change: if the stall cleared with dep-6010 still live and settlement on schema v1, the deserialization-mismatch mechanism would not explain the outage.

A consumer-group rebalance/partition-assignment-loss or offset-commit-failure signature found in the unreturned settlement-service logs, or a broker-side rebalance/partition event near 07:40Z, which would support H3 and weaken the poison-record explanation.
Evidence of ledger-db latency or error-rate degradation coinciding with onset (metrics not currently exposed) that would make H4 an active co-factor.
Proof that cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) alone, without any schema mismatch, blocks a partition or blocks offset commits, which would raise H2.
Evidence that the affected record never actually carried the legacy 'qty' field mismatch - i.e. that the error text was misattributed and the failure arises from a different mechanism.
